newsitem.title: UK: RESEARCH ALERT - Kleinwort lifts Granada forecasts. [CORRECTED 11:58 GMT]
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Kleinwort lifts Granada forecasts. [CORRECTED 11:58 GMT]

text.p: Dresdner Kleinwort Benson said on Monday it had upgraded its 1998 and 1999 profit forecasts for Granada Group Plc, based on the potential benefits from the company's disposal programme.
DKB is forecasting 1997 pre-tax profit for Granada of 644 million pounds, up from 480 million in 1996.
It has raised its 1998 estimate from 748 million (corrects from "740 million") to 760 million and is looking for a 1999 figure of 842.5 million, against a previous forecast of 830 million pounds.
"We are factoring in disposal proceeds much more explicitly," said analyst Paul Slattery. "We have not changed any of our basic trading assumptions," he added.
DKB repeated its "buy" recommendation on Granada stocks. Granada shares were unchanged at 912.5p at 1100 GMT.

DKB's central case is based on the disposal of 13 of Granada's 17 Exclusive Hotels, its Welcome Break motorway service stations, plus its stakes in Savoy Hotel and Alpha Airports in the current year for a total of 1.16 billion pounds.
It sees various disposals in 1997/98 for 140 million pounds.
Granada has so far sold three of the Exclusive properties it acquired as part of last year's takeover of Forte. It has also disposed of its 25 percent Alpha stake for 52 million pounds.
